# The rem Unit

#### Course: Learn CSS

## The rem Unit

The rem (root em) unit is similar to em—it's based on the font size of the root element (usually the <html> element) rather than the parent element.

Example

```html
1<html>
2    <p class="p1">This is 1rem</p>
3    <p class="p2">This is 2rem</p>
4</html>
```

```css
1html {
2    font-size: 32px;
3}
4
5.p1 {
6    font-size: 1rem;
7}
8
9.p2 {
10    font-size: 2rem;
11}
```

Browser Output

![rem Units](data:image/png;base64,)

In this case,

- The font size of <html> is set to 32px.
- p1 with 1rem has a font size of 1 × 32px = 32px.
- p2 with 2rem has a font size of 2 × 32px = 64px.

Unlike em, rem units always refer to the root font size, so they're handy when you want a consistent font size across a page.
